text:
marissa: Heads up — customer A is prepping a private/on‑prem deployment. Need guidance on a limited RBAC change so the ops team can rotate KMS keys without full admin, plus the network isolation checklist and the audit log format we should expect. cc @anika @leo

anika: Short answer: create a dedicated role `kms-key-rotation` that only allows key rotation and relevant logging. No IAM admin perms. Keep crypto ops separate from infra. Minimal policy (pseudo):
```json
{
  \"action\": \"allow\",
  \"resource\": \"kms/keys/*\",
  \"permissions\": [\"kms.keys.rotate\", \"kms.keys.get\"],
  \"conditions\": {\"require_mfa\": true, \"approved_principals\": [\"group:crypto-ops\"]}
}
```
Add logs:write to forward rotation events to SIEM. Audit fields we care about: `principal`, `action`, `resource`, `timestamp`, `session_id`, `outcome`.

leo: Network checklist (short): control plane + admin UI in private subnet; egress allowlist only to KMS endpoints + SIEM + our update servers; deny all other egress. Host firewall + CNI policy (Calico) to enforce pod-to-pod and pod-to-external rules. No direct hostNetwork apps unless reviewed.

jonathan: Also enforce mTLS between control-plane components and require client certs for agents. Short-lived session tokens (rotate hourly) and include `session_id` in every audit event. Alerts on failed rotation attempts.

marissa: For air-gapped/offline KMS options — customer asked if we support HSMs and manual key import flows. Thoughts?

anika: Airgap pattern we recommend: offline root HSM that performs key wrapping. Flow: generate model/data key on host, request HSM to wrap the CEK (content encryption key), record wrap metadata and sign a manifest, then transfer wrapped blob into the cluster via secured media. Keep an auditable manifest signed by the HSM. No unwrapped key leaves an HSM boundary. Documented playbook required.

leo: Quick Calico NetworkPolicy example (pseudo) to allow only KMS and SIEM egress from control-plane pods:
```yaml
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: GlobalNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: controlplane-egress-restrict
spec:
  selector: app == 'control-plane'
  egress:
    - action: Allow
      destination:
        nets: ["10.10.20.0/24"] # kms cluster
        ports: [443]
    - action: Allow
      destination:
        nets: ["10.20.30.0/24"] # siem
        ports: [443]
  order: 100
  types: [Egress]
```
Replace nets with customer-managed IPs.

jonathan: SIEM rules we should add: detect key-rotation events from unknown principals, spikes in `kms.keys.rotate` frequency, rotation attempts outside business hours, and any rotation where `outcome != success`. Example: alert if >3 failed rotate requests in 10m from same principal.

devsecops-bot: NOTE: New role template created: `kms-key-rotation` v1.0 — /templates/kms-key-rotation (internal link).

marissa: I'll open a ticket to provision the role and schedule the network lockdown changes. Also will kick off a vuln triage on the on‑prem images (noticed busybox in init container) before customer rollout.

anika: For audit retention & compliance: store immutable append-only logs (WORM) and encrypt with KMS. Keep replication/offsite copies and signed manifests. For enterprise customers, retention default 7 years but configurable. Make sure SIEM ingests `session_id` and `principal_email` for SSO mapping.

jonathan: Incident runbook notes (short): suspected KMS compromise -> 1) isolate control plane (deny egress), 2) revoke keys and rotate wrapped CEKs, 3) revoke agent certs and issue short-lived replacements, 4) run full access audit, 5) notify customer + compliance. I'll attach step-by-step to the ticket.

marissa: Great. I'll coordinate dry‑run with the customer next week. Ping me if you want to join the tabletop.

security-audit-bot: Audit reminder: ensure `kms-key-rotation` role has an annual access review and that rotation actions are hooked to an immutable audit store.
